newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions say Deputies against labor bill.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions say Deputies against labor bill.

text.p: Argentina's Rodolfo Daer, head of the main CGT labor federation, said Monday that ruling Peronist Party legislators have assured him they would not endorse the government's labor reform package being sent to Congress this week.

"We already have the opinions of the various parliamentary groups, including the Peronists, that say they are not going to guarantee any initiative that threatens employment," Daer told a local radio station.
He added that President Carlos Menem, who faces stiff resistance to his labor reforms, "has not started this debate to resolve the problems of unemployment and economic recovery."

The trade unionist, whose group organized a 36-hour general strike last week to protest the government's austerity policies, said the real intention of the government with its labor reforms is to reduce salaries.

The government's labor reforms include changes to collective wage bargaining by workers, flexibilization of working hours and holidays, the creation of lay-off funds and variable salaries depending on the firm's productivity.
Menem has said that the labor reforms will reduce unemployment from its current 17.1 percent rate to seven percent in two or three years.
